newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Lawyers group to assist in Rwanda genocide trials.
newsitem.headline: Lawyers group to assist in Rwanda genocide trials.

text.p: An international lawyers group warned on Tuesday that there was a serious shortage of lawyers for trials related to the 1994 genocide in Rwanda and vowed to ensure justice for all by sending in international legal teams.
Avocats sans Frontieres (Lawyers without Frontiers) said it expected the trials to start in the first half of next year.
"But one of the leading actors could well be missing: the lawyer...representing the victim or assisting the culprit," AsF said in a statement.

AsF chairman Pierre Legros told a news conference that an estimated 80,000 people were jailed pending trial. But at the same time the 1994 massacres had reduced the number of Rwandan lawyers to between 20 and 30.
"Without lawyers there can be no full trial," said Legros.
AsF will initially send four lawyers to Rwanda to assist four Rwandan lawyers at the first trials, which are expected to start within three to four months.
Afterwards a rota system of 10 lawyers per month would be implemented for which hundreds of candidates were required.

Legros said Belgium has earmarked 46 million francs for the project, called Justice for All in Rwanda. AsF is also banking on support from the European Union, the United Nations and countries like Switzerland.
"This is a temporary project in which we hope to restore the basic legal structures (in Rwanda) as soon as possible and start up the flow of trials," AsF co-secretary general Jean Flamme said.
"This is a major challenge... those 80,000 will more than probably also include innocent people, children," he said.
Co-secretary general Jacques Van Gelder said it was impossible to predict how long the trials would last but that AsF would send lawyers for about one year before assessing the situation.
Flamme said the Rwandan government had vowed to start the trials as soon as possible.
"We didn't set any deadline...we know how difficult it is to set up a judicial structure from less than scratch. Training magistrates in two months is almost a mission impossible," he said.
Van Gelder said AsF welcomed news that a new Rwandan bar could be set up before the end of the year. "We're ready to help set up a free and independent professional structure." he said.
He said one of the biggest problems facing the lawyers would be language and he noted that the trials would take place throughout the country and not just in the capital Kigali.
"Depending on the situation we can send additional teams," he said.
Lawyers volunteering for the project would first be trained in Rwandan law and the social, political and economic situation in the country, AsF said.
The Brussels-based lawyers group was established in January 1991 and says it represents lawyers and attorneys from all parts of the world.
